question: When was the Indian Official Secrets Act passed which restricted the freedom of the press?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 1904.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Official Secrets Act** was enacted in **1904** as a measure to curb dissent and restrict the freedom of the press in colonial India.
 
• The act criminalized the unauthorized disclosure of official secrets, thereby limiting journalists' ability to report on government activities.
 
• It was a tool used by the British authorities to suppress any form of opposition and maintain control over information dissemination.
 
• The act has undergone amendments and remains a significant law in India, raising debates about press freedom and state security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context**: The act was passed during a time of rising nationalist sentiments in India, where the British sought to quell any potential uprising through restrictive laws.
 
• **Provisions of the Act**: It included penalties for espionage and the disclosure of official information deemed sensitive, impacting not only journalists but also ordinary citizens.
 
• **Contemporary Relevance**: The Indian Official Secrets Act continues to be relevant today, often cited in discussions about the balance between national security and the right to information.
 
• **Criticism**: Over the years, the act has faced criticism for being misused to silence critics of the government and curtail the rights of the press.
